channel.title: The Brief — Adam's News
channel.description: Every story from Adam's three daily briefs (9 AM / 5 PM / 10 PM CT) as its own item, readable right in your feed reader, with a link to the original article.

item.title: Zelensky pushes for trilateral talks "no later than early November" — sooner than Moscow's "after Nov. 10"
item.description: After the St. Petersburg readout landed in the evening brief (Putin agreed "in principle" to trilateral talks after Nov. 10, at technical level), Zelensky told journalists on his way back to Kyiv that Ukraine supports a US proposal for three-way talks at negotiator level "as soon as possible, preferably no later than early November." He said Kyiv has feedback that Russia supports a trilateral meeting at negotiating-team level, and that the US "will do everything to ensure that the meeting takes place as early as possible, in November." He also said Kyiv supports "any proposals for a ceasefire, an end to the war, an energy ceasefire as well as humanitarian initiatives." So the two sides are now publicly aligned on the format — but not yet on the date, and not on whether Putin himself ever sits at the table. Reuters Source: reuters.com.

item.title: Poland: quiet
US orders diplomats and families out of Saudi Arabia as Houthi strikes hit an airport and an oilfield in one day
item.description: The State Department ordered the departure of non-emergency US government employees and their family members from Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, and US officials told Reuters it plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions across the Gulf. Spokesman Tommy Pigott cited Houthi attacks "on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions." The order came after two deadly attacks Wednesday: one person killed and eight injured at Dammam's King Fahd International Airport, and two killed at Aramco's Shaybah oilfield (see below). The US Embassy in Riyadh also issued a security alert warning of possible further Houthi attacks. This is the sharpest US step yet in the Saudi-Houthi escalation — a formal ordered departure, not just a travel warning. Reuters via Devdiscourse · Reuters (Dammam) Source: devdiscourse.com.

item.title: Dammam airport attack kills 1, injures 8 — the second civilian airport hit in the Houthi campaign
item.description: Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on Wednesday evening killed one resident and injured eight others, with material damage still being assessed. It follows the deadly Riyadh airport strikes earlier this month and extends the Houthi airport campaign to the Gulf coast city of Dammam. Attribution details beyond the Houthi campaign context were not specified in the Saudi statement. Reuters Source: reuters.com.

item.title: Follow-up: Shaybah deaths now confirmed by the Saudi Energy Ministry — 2 killed, 2 injured by falling debris
item.description: What the evening brief flagged as single-source is now confirmed: Saudi air defences intercepted a drone targeting Aramco's Shaybah oilfield on Wednesday, and falling debris killed two residents — one Filipino, one Nepali — and injured two more, one Pakistani and one Indian. Debris set a contractor's vehicle on fire outside the facility's perimeter; the ministry said operations at the field were not affected. BOE Report (Reuters wire) Source: boereport.com.

item.title: Oil climbs again on the departure order — Brent back above $110
item.description: Brent rose $1.29 (1.2%) to $110.11 in early Thursday trading after settling largely unchanged Wednesday, with WTI up to $98.12, as the US departure order and the Dammam/Shaybah attacks renewed supply fears. Kpler data cited by Reuters counts at least 18 shipping attacks over the past two weeks, and LSEG analysts warn Iran is now targeting tankers well beyond the strait, into the Gulf of Oman, threatening loadings and ship-to-ship transfers. Reuters Source: reuters.com.

item.title: Explosions heard in Sirik, southern Iran — origin unknown, developing
item.description: Iranian media reported explosions heard in Sirik in southern Iran on Wednesday, saying the nature and origin were unknown. No claim or official explanation had surfaced by brief time — treat as developing, not as a confirmed strike. Reuters --- Source: reuters.com.

item.title: Fortnite returns to Apple's Australian App Store on Thursday after court-ordered iOS opening
item.description: Epic Games said Wednesday that Fortnite will return to Apple's App Store in Australia on Thursday, after the country's federal court found Apple violated competition law and ordered it to open up iOS. A related ruling formalized that Apple must open its iOS ecosystem to rival app distribution and payment systems for Australian account holders, with most changes taking effect by March 1, 2027 — but Epic lost its bid for global remedies, and the court declined to find any particular developer or user was overcharged, leaving compensation unresolved. Reuters via WIXX · MLex Source: wixx.com.

item.title: Google brings conversational Gemini navigation to Apple CarPlay in the US
item.description: Google rolled out conversational Gemini inside Google Maps on Apple CarPlay to US users on Thursday, nearly a year after the assistant landed on Android Auto. Drivers can talk to Gemini directly in Maps — multi-step questions like restaurant suggestions followed by directions avoiding toll roads, plus hands-free traffic reports. Global availability is promised but undated, and — unlike Wednesday's Android Auto rollout — there's no mention yet of the Personal Intelligence features that pull from Gmail, Calendar and Photos. AI Daily Post Source: aidailypost.com.

item.title: Nvidia: quiet overnight
Nvidia's DeepStream 9.2 puts more of the video-analytics stack in the open
item.description: DeepStream 9.2 shipped Wednesday with a bigger open-source footprint: the monorepo now includes 12 GStreamer elements and 30+ libraries as source, including the nvv4l2 codecs and Re-ID vision and text embedding plugins. The release adds intelligent frame selection (send only the most relevant frames to vision-language models), an active-learning pipeline with runtime model switching, and GB300 support plus JetPack 7.2.1 for Jetson Thor/Orin. NVIDIA Developer Forums Source: forums.developer.nvidia.com.

item.title: Storytold's Rust Office and CAD clones keep climbing — Wordcraft ~15,300 stars, CADcraft ~6,300
item.description: The clean-room Rust reimplementations from the same team behind the earlier ArtCraft Adobe clones are still trending: Wordcraft (Microsoft Word alternative) is at roughly 15,300 stars after gaining ~291 in a day, and CADcraft (AutoCAD-style drafting) at roughly 6,300 after ~168 in a day. Both are early-stage and worth watching as alternatives, not yet as replacements. GitDiscover --- Source: gitdiscover.org.

item.title: Follow-up: PHP2Shell exploitation is now being observed in the wild — still no KEV listing
item.description: The evening brief's patch-now warning got sharper overnight: watchTowr says it is now observing in-the-wild exploitation attempts against the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both CVSS 9.2), with a variety of hastily built proof-of-concept exploits hitting its sensors — none successful yet, in its assessment, but "we don't expect that will last long." CISA issued an overnight alert urging immediate patching to 8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35, and Australia's cyber centre issued an urgent warning late Oct. 21. The scale problem: roughly 79–80% of PHP sites run versions that no longer receive support, so for them there is no official patch — only upgrade, isolation, or a WAF as a stopgap. Neither CVE was in CISA's KEV catalog in the reports checked. Cyber Daily · SC Media Source: cyberdaily.au.

item.title: Follow-up: LiteLLM fallout — check for two telltale files if you installed 1.107.0
item.description: More detail on Wednesday's hijacked LiteLLM release: security researchers say anyone who installed or ran 1.107.0 should check for /tmp/.pc_once_* (meaning the credential exfiltration already fired) and /tmp/remote_code_loader.lock (meaning the remote-code loader daemon ran or is still running). LiteLLM — an open-source gateway routing to 100+ model providers, at roughly 23 million weekly downloads — pulled the release within hours, and the last safe release remains 1.106.2. If either file is present, treat every credential the machine could reach as compromised and rotate. Pivot News · Tesla News Wire --- Source: pivotnews.ai.

item.title: Russell Brand trial: final complainant's evidence concludes — jury sent home until Thursday
item.description: At Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday, the final complainant (Woman 5) completed her evidence. Under cross-examination she maintained she did not consent to the alleged 2009 anal rape, and on re-examination by prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC she answered "Absolutely not" when asked whether having anal sex with Brand was a decision she made — "That was the whole reason for going to the police." She told jurors Brand "acted like nothing had happened" afterward. The jury was sent home until Thursday morning. Brand denies all seven charges (3 rapes, 3 sexual assaults, 1 indecent assault, 1999–2009); the trial continues. The Times live blog Source: thetimes.com.

item.title: Putin agrees "in principle" to trilateral talks after Nov. 10 — but not at the leaders' table
item.description: The readout from the Witkoff–Putin meeting finally landed this afternoon: Kremlin foreign-policy adviser Yuri Ushakov said Putin agreed "in principle" that trilateral US–Russia–Ukraine talks will continue after Nov. 10, focused on "building a security system for Russia and Ukraine after the conflict ends." A US official added the talks would happen "at the technical level" — meaning Putin himself won't sit down with Trump or Zelensky. Both sides accepted the trilateral format (Ukraine in Oslo Tuesday, Russia in St. Petersburg today), and the US readout cited "progress" on a post-war economic plan and European security architecture. The catch, per CNN: no indication Russia has budged on its maximalist positions — full Donbas, a shrunken Ukrainian military, no NATO. Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev separately said the US–Russia diesel deal goes ahead despite European criticism. CNN · NY Post Source: cnn.com.

item.title: Zelensky: "freeze and stop" — he'd accept a deal that freezes the current front lines
item.description: In a Fox & Friends interview Wednesday morning, Zelensky said yes to a peace deal that freezes the fighting where it stands, with Ukraine keeping "75% or more" of its territory: "Right now we have to freeze, and I think this is (the) real way to end this war. We call it a ceasefire… freeze and stop." He called that the minimum needed from Russia, followed by US and European security guarantees so "the occupation will not return." He drew a line at giving up the Donbas — "not fair" — and at any deal negotiated without Ukraine ("don't speak about us without us"). It's a notable shift from his long-held rejection of frozen conflicts, and it landed hours before Putin's own "in principle" answer. NY Post · CNN Source: nypost.com.

item.title: Hubbard freed and heading to a Texas military hospital
item.description: The one concrete outcome of the St. Petersburg meeting: 74-year-old retired teacher Stephen Hubbard, detained since April 2022 and sentenced as an alleged mercenary, was released and photographed with Witkoff at the airport. CBS reported he will fly to Texas for medical treatment at a military hospital; he is in poor health after more than four years in Russian custody. NY Post Source: nypost.com.

item.title: Poland: quiet
Iran–US deadlock, stated plainly by both sides: no talks under blockade, no relief while ships are attacked
item.description: Iranian President Pezeshkian said Wednesday the US "cannot expect dialogue" while imposing a blockade and issuing threats. Foreign Minister Araghchi, in a Financial Times op-ed, said Iran would give diplomacy "another chance" if it sees "strong evidence of a sincere desire" for a just solution — and urged a return to the June Islamabad memorandum, under which Iran would reopen the strait and the US would lift the blockade, release frozen oil funds and remove sanctions. Washington isn't biting: Secretary of State Rubio told US media a deal would be "extremely difficult" and economic pressure continues until Iran stops targeting commercial shipping. Indirect backchannels via Pakistan and Qatar are reportedly still active, but nothing is confirmed. Bloomberg via Military.com · AnewZ Source: military.com.

item.title: Shaybah oilfield: Saudi defences intercepted a drone — and one outlet reports two killed
item.description: Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said air defences intercepted a drone attempting to hit a facility at Aramco's Shaybah oilfield in the Eastern Region. A breaking-news outlet separately reported two people killed in a drone attack on Shaybah with no operational impact — that death toll is single-source and unconfirmed, so treat it as developing. Shaybah is one of the sites the Houthis claimed to have hit Monday; Saudi sources denied those claims, saying the facilities are intact. for-ex.news (intercept + reported deaths) Source: for-ex.news.

item.title: Google Cloud's Vera Rubin A5X instances go live — general availability in November, up to 960,000 Rubin GPUs planned
item.description: Announced at GTC Berlin on Wednesday: the first live A5X instances, built on Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 racks with ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google's Virgo Network and fourth-generation liquid cooling, are running with an initial customer — Ineffable Intelligence, the London lab founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver, which is using them for reinforcement-learning systems that learn from experience. General availability comes next month, with expansion to Europe planned, and Google Cloud says it plans to scale Vera Rubin infrastructure to as many as 960,000 GPUs across multiple sites (a stated plan, not installed capacity). WPP also demoed a creative-agent reference architecture on A5X with Nvidia Nemotron models and OpenShell, with multi-node workloads running on a single instance in initial tests. Unite.AI · Tesla News Wire Source: unite.ai.

item.title: Apple confirms "limited" iPhone Duo walk-in stock for Friday — and Gurman calls the preorder timing a "major mistake"
item.description: Apple told MacRumors and 9to5Mac that stores will have limited Duo units for walk-in customers on Friday's Oct. 23 launch in the US, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Mexico, Germany, the Netherlands, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Türkiye, the UK and most stores in Italy (Macao: launch-day walk-ins only, limited). No walk-in sales in France, China, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand or the UAE — reservation-only pickup there. Apple expects the limited stock to sell out quickly; AppleInsider reports new pre-orders are now showing January 25, 2027 delivery. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, in his Power On newsletter, called launching pre-orders Oct. 16 despite known "severe supply constraints" a "major mistake." MacRumors · 9to5Mac · AppleInsider --- Source: images.macrumors.com.

item.title: Follow-up: DeepInfer keeps climbing — ~17,500 stars by Wednesday evening Berlin time

The caveats from the morning brief still stand: no independent benchmarks yet, and the release omits a KV-cache system, prefill/decode disaggregation and replica load balancing. djcroman Source: djcroman.com.

item.title: Railtracks Swift ADK goes open source under MIT
item.description: Railtown AI open-sourced its Railtracks Swift agent-development kit on GitHub under the MIT licence, extending its existing Python framework into Apple's native environment. It supports agent reasoning, tool invocation, structured outputs, multi-agent orchestration, execution tracing and guardrails, with OpenAI, Anthropic and Google Gemini providers plus on-device Apple Intelligence. Company announcement — adoption is the thing to watch, not the press release. Kalkine --- Source: kalkine.ca.

item.title: PHP2Shell: emergency patches out today for two critical PHP flaws — NSA, FBI and CISA say patch now or take systems offline
item.description: PHP released fixes Wednesday (8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35) for CVE-2026-109618 (RCE via out-of-memory corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (RCE via stale global state), both CVSS 9.2, both allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. The release was pulled forward a day after details leaked on Hacker News ahead of the planned Oct. 22 disclosure. Apache mod_php is at highest risk — PHP says a demonstrated exploit triggers before application code runs — but FPM, CGI, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed are also at risk. NSA, FBI and CISA urged immediate patching or taking unpatched systems offline; Unit 42 counts 22.6M+ internet-exposed instances potentially vulnerable. Cloudflare says it is already seeing early attack attempts and has deployed WAF rules; watchTowr honeypots logged exploitation attempts; several European government sites went offline to patch. CISA had not observed exploitation as of publication, and neither CVE is on KEV yet — but exploit code is circulating publicly, so this is a patch-now, not patch-soon, item. Defense One · SC Media · Tenable FAQ Source: defenseone.com.

item.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 was hijacked on PyPI for ~1¾ hours — a credential stealer in one of AI's most-used plumbing packages
item.description: BerriAI confirmed its LiteLLM 1.107.0 release, published to PyPI and Docker on Wednesday, "contained compiled malware which steals credentials and loads remote-code execution tools." Attackers used three engineers' GitHub accounts via apparently stolen GitHub CLI tokens, overrode branch protection, and built the release from a lookalike "Berri-AI" copy of the repo. Seven malicious wheels were live on PyPI 11:39–13:23 UTC; tainted Docker images (including latest) stayed up until 14:20 UTC. The payload steals SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI/CD secrets, browser passwords and LLM provider keys, and runs on any Python startup — even without importing litellm. Wiz already observed stolen AWS credentials being validated from 16:20 UTC, consistent with LLMjacking. If you installed or ran 1.107.0, rotate everything it could have touched; 1.106.2 and the release candidates are clean. This is LiteLLM's second hijack this year. BerriAI incident report · Wiz · Socket --- Source: docs.litellm.ai.

item.title: Russell Brand trial: final complainant's recorded interview played — "you treated me like an animal"
item.description: At Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday, jurors heard the recorded police interview of the final complainant, who alleges Brand anally raped her at his home in 2009 after consensual sex began. She described a later text exchange, about six months after the alleged incident, in which she told him he had "treated her like an animal" and he replied "I'm sorry" — and said she was left feeling "really degraded" and "like a piece of meat." Brand's lawyer put it to her that she had agreed to the act, suggesting she was "young, impressionable and obsessed" with him. Brand denies all seven charges (3 rapes, 3 sexual assaults, 1 indecent assault, 1999–2009); the ~6-week trial continues. Reuters via Devdiscourse · The Times live blog Source: devdiscourse.com.

item.title: Witkoff met Putin in St. Petersburg for ~3 hours — and Russia released an American prisoner
item.description: US envoy Steve Witkoff carried the Oslo framework to Vladimir Putin on Wednesday morning at Constantine Palace, pushing to reopen direct US–Russia–Ukraine trilateral talks. The Kremlin said the talks lasted about three hours, with no immediate comment afterward from either side. One concrete outcome did emerge: Witkoff announced Russia released 74-year-old American prisoner Stephen Hubbard, detained for more than four years. The agenda also covered Russia helping resolve the Iran war and potential Russian fertilizer exports to the US. Moscow, meanwhile, struck a cool tone in advance — Lavrov said Russia "does not expect a miracle" and will not make "political concessions." Zelensky's line before the meeting: "Let's see what Putin has to say," and that much depends on whether Washington hears "something new from Russia today — about peace, rather than the continuation of the war." CNN · AP via Military.com · Devdiscourse Source: cnn.com.

item.title: Overnight Russian strikes killed 4 and hit energy sites in four regions
item.description: Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said overnight strikes hit power facilities in the Kyiv, Volyn, Odesa and Mykolaiv regions, plus civilian enterprises in at least two others. A drone slammed into a 24-story apartment building in Kyiv, killing two; in Korotych, outside Kharkiv, strikes killed an 81-year-old woman and an 83-year-old man and injured 11, including two children. A university building and a shopping centre in central Ukraine were also hit, with injuries reported in Poltava, Lviv, Cherkasy and Chernihiv. Russia's defence ministry gave a different account: a drone-storage warehouse complex in Poltava, the Nivki substation in Kyiv, and a cargo ship carrying military cargo to Odesa. Reuters via 94.1 Duke FM · The Orbit Post Source: 941theduke.com.

item.title: First Russian diesel tanker to the US sails Thursday — the Trump diesel deal, made concrete
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia will send its first 40,000-ton diesel tanker to the US on Thursday, with more shipments to follow. That's the delivery mechanism behind the deal at the center of the last two weeks of US–Ukraine friction — and it lands the morning after Witkoff's Putin meeting. Oilprice Source: oilprice.com.

item.title: Starshield row sharpens: WSJ says Musk ordered the slowdown; Rubio says it's Musk's call, not the White House's
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that Elon Musk ordered the speed slowdown on Starshield, Ukraine's military-grade Starlink service, after discussions with Trump and White House officials — one source said beforehand, two said in the days after. On Wednesday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said decisions on Ukraine's Starlink access are up to SpaceX and Musk, not the White House, calling it "governed by a private commercial contract" — an apparent shift from his earlier position that no one ordered a slowdown. Defence Secretary Hegseth said Tuesday the Pentagon "hasn't pulled anything back" and issued no directives. Meanwhile the practical problem is unresolved: reporting says Ukrainian drones still cannot fly faster than 130 km/h without losing connection. Zelensky said Tuesday that US early warnings are working again; the Starshield question is separate and still open. Reuters via 94.1 Duke FM · Pollar News Source: 941theduke.com.

item.title: Poland: quiet
Houthis deny any drones toward Medina on Wednesday — after the coalition said it intercepted them there
item.description: Yemen's Houthis said they launched no drones toward the holy city of Medina on Wednesday and conducted no military operations toward Saudi Arabia at all, denying the Saudi-led coalition's claim that it intercepted drones over Medina and the Eastern region. The denial matters because the Houthis had previously said Mecca and Medina airspace would be exempt from their airline warning — a Medina strike claim, if true, would cross their own red line. Within Yemen, the Houthis claimed an attack Wednesday on a military camp near Aden airport, and a government source told Reuters they also attacked Riyan airport in Mukalla. Attribution on the Medina/Eastern intercepts is contested — developing. Reuters via Devdiscourse Source: devdiscourse.com.

item.title: Coalition says it destroyed the launcher behind a Riyadh-bound ballistic missile
item.description: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed the launch platform used to fire a Houthi ballistic missile toward Riyadh, after earlier announcing the missile itself was intercepted. No location or operational details were given. Al Arabiya via Aalimi Nation Source: aalimination.com.

item.title: New tanker hit off Oman overnight — fire out, crew safe, attacker unidentified
item.description: UKMTO reported that at about 0145 GMT Wednesday, an unidentified projectile hit a tanker roughly 11 nautical miles west of Buha, Oman. The fire was later put out, the tanker is at anchor, the entire crew is safe, and no environmental impact was reported. A separate Tuesday incident saw a projectile hit a tanker 30 nautical miles from Al Faw, Iraq, with no casualties and no damage. The pattern keeps widening beyond the strait itself into the Gulf of Oman. Srpske Novine (UKMTO) Source: srpske.rs.

item.title: Bloomberg: Iran's ship attacks are getting more frequent and more damaging — engine rooms now the target
item.description: At least 23 incidents involving ships attacked in or near Hormuz were logged in the first two weeks of October, with at least five reporting engine-room impacts, according to naval groups and security consultants. Engine-room hits cause fires and leave ships without power or propulsion for months of repairs — an echo of the 1980s Tanker War. Officials say Iran has shifted from drones to missiles, which steer toward hotter parts of a ship and carry larger payloads. The IRGC on Tuesday claimed a third tanker in days — a supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels — exploded on a mine south of the strait after switching off radar and navigation; that claim remains unconfirmed, and CENTCOM has disputed the earlier mine claims. US Energy Secretary Wright said Sunday shipments are at about 80% of normal — against IMF PortWatch's 4 transits on Oct 18 vs ~85/day baseline. Bloomberg via Rigzone · Malay Mail (IRGC claim) Source: rigzone.com.

item.title: Oil back above $110 as talks rumours fade and US stocks draw down
item.description: Brent rose 1.5% to $110.38 in early Wednesday trading (WTI $99.18) after settling Tuesday at $108.79 off a five-month high of $111.99. Tuesday's dip came on unconfirmed reports of Qatar- and Pakistan-brokered mediation — Pakistan's army chief met Iranian leaders in Tehran on Oct 20 — but Iranian outlet Nournews reported Iran saying there would be no talks until its demands are met, and no official confirmation of a Qatari delegation emerged. API data showed US crude stocks fell 4.9 million barrels last week, on top of an 11.12 million draw the week before. Araghchi reiterated the strait stays closed until Washington accepts Tehran's seven-day plan; indirect talks via Pakistan and Qatar are reported to be continuing, but nothing is confirmed. Reuters via 106.5 Jack FM --- Source: jack1065.com.

item.title: Nvidia GTC Berlin keynote: OpenShell to leash AI agents, DSX POD factories in 14 days, Vera Rubin in full production
item.description: Jensen Huang's keynote Wednesday unveiled the OpenShell Reference Architecture — models think on Vera Rubin systems, agent tool-use runs on Vera CPUs, and BlueField-4 chips run Sentry software to watch agent behavior from outside the system and enforce policy in hardware — plus DSX POD, prebuilt container AI factories Nvidia says cut onsite deployment from six months to 14 days, with deliveries worldwide in early 2027. Nvidia says Vera Rubin is in full production, its European commitments now approach $10 billion, and its DSX designs can cut cooling water use by up to 100%. The Register's caveat, noted in coverage: OpenShell requires Nvidia hardware, still has open security issues on GitHub, and collects telemetry by default unless users opt out. Separately, Nvidia announced an Isaac robotics expansion — a reference humanoid (Agile ONE SN, 1.40m, 31 degrees of freedom, Jetson Thor onboard), Isaac OS runtime and Isaac Lab 3.0 — and supply-chain capacity expansion including 2.5x substrate capacity over three years. Tesla News Wire · GlobeNewswire via Morningstar (Isaac) · GlobeNewswire via Morningstar (supply chain) Source: teslanewswire.com.

item.title: iPhone Duo reviews are out: "coolest phone in years" — but apps aren't ready for it
item.description: First reviews landed Wednesday ahead of Friday's Oct 23 launch: CNN's verdict is that the $2,000 foldable is genuinely fun — giant inner screen (near iPad mini size), doubles as bedside clock, mini monitor and tripod camera — but many apps still aren't built for the big screen, and developers haven't updated them yet. Apple also capped US pre-orders at two units per customer, after reports that launch-day walk-in stock will be effectively nil. CNN · Gadgets360 Source: cnn.com.

item.title: Google rolls Gemini Personal Intelligence out to Android Auto today
item.description: Gemini in the car can now pull from Gmail, Calendar, Photos, Maps, YouTube and Search with the user's permission — ask for a flight gate and on-time status in one question, navigate to a doctor's appointment without the address, or find a car wash from a photo taken last week. It's opt-in (auto-on if already enabled in the Gemini app), rolling out on Android Auto starting today; cars with Google built-in get it in the coming months. Excluded: Workspace accounts, and the EEA, Switzerland, the UK and Nigeria. FoneArena --- Source: fonearena.com.

item.title: AfD email leak: 421,179 internal emails (281 GB) published on hexane.cc
item.description: AfD confirmed Oct 19 that a hosting provider was hacked in September and mailboxes copied.
